title: Ghost policy shadowing causes Hosted requests to route to incompatible Dedicated models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A set of recent customer escalations show Hosted API traffic being silently routed to Dedicated pools running incompatible model binaries (different tokenizer/config). This resulted in garbled output and a P0 support incident for a high-value customer (Acme Chat). The routing decision appears to come from an out-of-order policy overlay that 'shadows' the intended tenant routing policy during concurrent policy updates and syncs between control plane and edge routers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate two rapid policy changes for tenant T: (a) add dedicated-pool affinity, (b) toggle a regional override. Apply them within 200ms of each other.
2) Push a request to Hosted endpoint for tenant T that expects hosted-tier model A (tokenizer v1).
3) Observe the request being routed to a Dedicated pool running model variant B (tokenizer v2) and returning invalid tokens/errors.
4) Reproduce via canary cluster by replaying policy update sequence from recorded prod events (see monitoring link).
recent_updates: 2026-03-01 - Ticket created after support escalation from Acme Chat; initial triage assigned to Marco.
2026-03-02 - Collected policy-sync traces and request traces; observed mismatched policy_version between control plane and router (~2-3s window).
2026-03-04 - Reproduced misroute in staging using scripted concurrent policy pushes against the router; created minimal repro harness.
2026-03-06 - Identified race condition in policy merge: newest per-tenant overlay applied without checking per-request effective TTL leading to shadowed rules.
2026-03-08 - Deployed hotfix (routing-service v3.6.2-alpha) that adds version affinity check; running limited canary on staging infra.
2026-03-10 - Canary passed for 6h with no misroutes; preparing rollback-safe gradual rollout to prod and coordinating customer remediation.
Notes: support notified Acme Chat of mitigation steps (pin tenant to hosted-model A) and provided temporary routing rule to avoid Dedicated pools.
root_cause_analysis: Race in policy apply path: concurrent policy patches generated conflicting overlays. The router's merge logic used last-writer-wins but did not validate applicability to active request class (hosted vs dedicated).

Policy cache TTL semantics: router used a stale cache entry during the 2-3s window while a new overlay was being propagated from control plane. That stale entry included a deprecated affinity field pointing to a Dedicated pool.
Lack of tokenizer/model compatibility checks at routing time: router assumed model variants were functionally interchangeable and forwarded requests without verifying compatibility metadata.
Edge case triggered by customers who have both hosted usage and newly-provisioned Dedicated commitments with overlapping model names but incompatible builds.
fix_plan: Hotfix (done): add a policy_version check on the router so that an overlay only takes effect if it is fully synchronized and its applicable scope matches the request context (tier + region + tenant).
Hotfix (done): add a lightweight compatibility guard that rejects a routing target if model_metadata.tokenizer_version != request.expected_tokenizer_version; fall back to hosted model if mismatch.
Mid-term: rewrite policy merge algorithm to use explicit precedence levels (global < region < tenant < runtime) and serialize overlay application per-tenant to avoid races.
Add robust end-to-end tests in routing-integration suite that simulate concurrent policy updates and verify no misroutes across hosted/dedicated/private boundaries.
Add observability: emit misroute-warnings metric (labels: tenant, intended_tier, routed_tier, model_mismatch) and dashboard with 1m resolution and alert threshold.
Customer remediation: provide script for affected tenants to pin model version or temporarily opt-out of Dedicated affinity while fix is rolled out.
Postmortem & review: schedule blameless postmortem with PM, Support, SRE, and Product to align policy semantics and UI controls.
resolved_in_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4128 - router: enforce policy_version and scope checks
https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4145 - tests: add concurrent policy update scenarios
notes_and_tradeoffs: Compatibility checks add ~0.2ms median latency to routing decision path; acceptable for P0 mitigation but we should keep guard as optional for low-latency tiers.
Serializing per-tenant policy application reduces race but introduces a small window of decreased policy throughput during mass updates. We'll apply serialization only when overlay count > threshold.

We avoided a heavy-weight validation that queries Dedicated pool runtime for model metadata during every update to prevent cascading load on Dedicated control plane. Instead we cache model metadata with a short TTL (30s).
Long-term: consider normalizing model identifiers to include compatibility fingerprints so routing can be purely declarative.
acceptance_criteria: No production misroutes observed for 72h post-rollout in canary and prod regions for tenants with mixed hosted/dedicated usage.
Automated integration tests for concurrent policy updates pass in CI and are added to nightly regression run.
Telemetry emits misroute-warnings metric and alert is firing if rate > 1/min for any tenant; dashboard created and shared with SRE and Support.
Support notified affected customers and provided remediation steps; at least one customer (Acme Chat) confirmed improvements.
Postmortem published and reviewed with Product and Security (if required).
